drivingQuestion: How can Shabbat count as a single item when it has 39 labors each carrying an offering?
outcomeNote: R' Yochanan limits the mishna to a single-offering case

segments.he: הַמְחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת. אָמְרִי: שַׁבָּת אַרְבָּעִים חָסֵר אַחַת הָוְויָין! אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תַּנָּא שִׁגְגַת שַׁבָּת וּזְדוֹן מְלָאכוֹת, דְּלָא מִחַיַּיב אֶלָּא חֲדָא.
segments.en: § The mishna’s list of prohibitions for whose unwitting violation one must bring a sin offering includes «one who desecrates Shabbat.» The Sages express their surprise at this ruling and «say:» The primary labors of «Shabbat are forty-less-one,» and one is liable to bring a sin offering for each primary labor he violates. That alone totals more than the thirty-six cases mentioned in the mishna. «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» The tanna «taught» a case where his action was «unwitting with regard to Shabbat,» i.e., he was unaware it was Shabbat, «and» his action was «intentional with regard to» the prohibited «labors,» in that he was aware that the acts he performed were labors that are prohibited on Shabbat. In that case, the halakha is «that he is liable» to bring «only one» sin offering, as he committed only a single error.
